title: kate-syntax: context-stack highlighting engine with upstream golden tests
summary: The matching side. highlight_line takes a line and an interned start state, runs the rules of the top context left to right exactly like KSyntaxHighlighting's AbstractHighlighter::highlightLine (lookahead, firstNonSpace, column, dynamic captures, lineEndContext, lineEmptyContext, fallthrough, folding regions) and returns spans plus the end state. Golden tests reuse upstream autotests/input and autotests/reference for the vendored definitions, converted to our span format by a committed script output, so the Rust engine is held to the C++ engine's exact output. Per-rule delimiter overrides are not fields of Rule, and the loader drops them. This packet does not add those fields, because definition.rs is a forbidden path. The six MIT files do not set those overrides on a rule. Known limits: span columns are Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units. An included rule uses the word delimiters of the definition that includes it.

lane.reason: The hardest pure-logic packet in Phase 1 and the one with the best test oracle (upstream reference output). A large-context frontier model in the cloud, not a quantized local model.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: New modules. Dependencies with justification: fancy-regex (definitions use lookbehind and backreferences; the regex crate refuses them), smallvec (context stacks are short; avoid a heap allocation per line), lru (bounded cache for dynamic patterns).

regression_tests.name: golden::upstream_reference_output_matches
regression_tests.asserts: For each vendored definition with an upstream autotests/input file (MIT only), the span sequence per line equals the committed expected file derived from autotests/reference. Byte-for-byte, no tolerance.

regression_tests.name: engine::tests::highlight_is_deterministic_and_state_converges
regression_tests.asserts: Highlighting the same line twice from the same state yields identical output. The edit must change that line's end_state. Re-highlighting from the edited line then reaches a later line whose end_state equals the cached one.

regression_tests.name: engine::tests::lookahead_rule_consumes_nothing
regression_tests.asserts: A lookAhead RegExpr that switches context produces no span and the next rule in the new context matches at the same column.

regression_tests.name: regex::tests::unsupported_pattern_is_reported_at_load
regression_tests.asserts: A pattern using a PCRE verb such as (*SKIP) makes Highlighter::new return Err(RegexError::Unsupported). Construction does not panic.
